examples: a curving staircase
gently curving streets

source.twin_note_ru: curve чаще о плавном изгибе самой линии или дороги, bend обычно переходный: кто-то гнёт предмет

source.definition: having a round shape

a curved display/screen
a gently curved bay

The knife has a curved blade.
source.twin_note_ru: curved это форма по замыслу (curved screen), bent это погнутый, деформированный

source.definition: a US, Australian or New Zealand dollar; a South African rand; an Indian rupee

examples: They cost ten bucks.
We're talking big bucks (= a lot of money) here.
source.twin_note_ru: buck — разговорное, только в неформальной речи (twenty bucks); dollar — нейтральное и обязательное в официальных суммах и текстах.

source.definition: a friend

Howard and Mick were drinking buddies.

source.twin_note_ru: buddy — разговорное, американское, часто как обращение к незнакомцу (hey, buddy); friend — нейтральное в любом регистре.

source.definition: a feeling of great pleasure
source.example: a feeling of sheer/pure delight
examples: a feeling of sheer/pure delight

delight at something She couldn't hide her delight at the news.
delight at doing something He expressed his delight at seeing us all again.
source.twin_note_ru: delight это яркий восторг от чего-то конкретного; pleasure это удовольствие вообще, в том числе спокойное и привычное

source.definition: to give somebody a lot of pleasure and joy
source.example: This news will delight his fans all over the world.
examples: This news will delight his fans all over the world.
a movie that will thrill and delight most audiences
Her lack of reserve delighted him.
She had a limitless capacity to astonish and delight.
source.twin_note_ru: delight значит привести в восторг, эмоция сильная; please значит угодить, устроить человека, эмоция слабая

source.definition: very pleased
source.example: a delighted smile
examples: a delighted smile
delighted to do something I'd be absolutely delighted to come.
‘Can you stay for dinner?’ ‘I’d be delighted (to)!’
delighted that… I was delighted that you could stay.
delighted by something She was delighted by the news of the wedding.
delighted at something They were highly delighted at the court's decision.
delighted with something I was delighted with my presents.
delighted about something We are delighted about the decision.
delighted for somebody I was so pleased and delighted for him when he started losing weight.
source.twin_note_ru: delighted это «очень рад», сильно и вежливо-формально (I'd be delighted to); glad просто «доволен», обычно о мелочах

source.definition: a thing or person that reduces a shock or protects somebody/something against difficulties

examples: buffer against something, Support from family and friends acts as a buffer against stress.
buffer against something Support from family and friends acts as a buffer against stress.

The organization acts as a buffer between the management and the union.
a buffer state (= a small country between two powerful states that helps keep peace between them)
a buffer zone (= an area of land between two opposing armies or countries)
Peacekeepers have been sent in to establish a buffer zone between the rival forces.

source.definition: the main part of something; most of something
source.example: The bulk of the population lives in cities.
examples: The bulk of the population lives in cities.
The great bulk of the work has now been done.
source.twin_note_ru: bulk — большая часть массы или объёма (the bulk of the work), majority — большинство из счётного множества, особенно людей или голосов.

source.definition: a system of government in which the people of a country can vote to elect their representatives
source.example: parliamentary democracy
examples: parliamentary democracy
the principles of democracy
source.twin_note_ru: democracy это власть большинства через выборы; republic это форма правления без монарха, страна может быть республикой и без демократии

source.definition: controlled by representatives who are elected by the people of a country; connected with this system
source.example: a democratic country
examples: a democratic country
a democratic system
democratic government
They are aiming to make the institutions of the EU truly democratic.
Exercise your democratic right to vote.

source.definition: a large number of cases of a particular disease or medical condition happening at the same time in a particular community
source.example: the outbreak of a flu epidemic
examples: the outbreak of a flu epidemic
An epidemic of measles broke out, and over 200 children died.
Effectively, tobacco companies will be exporting an epidemic of smoking-related diseases, the campaign suggests.
source.twin_note_ru: epidemic: вспышка в одной стране или регионе, pandemic: та же болезнь, но охватившая многие страны.

source.definition: a duty, responsibility, etc. that causes worry, difficulty or hard work
source.example: to bear/carry/ease/reduce/share the burden
examples: to bear/carry/ease/reduce/share the burden
the burden (of something) The main burden of caring for old people falls on the state.
burden on somebody the heavy tax burden on working people
a burden to somebody I don't want to become a burden to my children when I'm old.
source.twin_note_ru: burden — чаще переносно: бремя, финансовая или моральная нагрузка; load — физический груз или конкретный объём работы.

source.definition: the system of official rules and ways of doing things that a government or an organization has, especially when these seem to be too complicated
source.example: unnecessary/excessive bureaucracy
examples: unnecessary/excessive bureaucracy
We need to reduce paperwork and bureaucracy in the company.

source.definition: a strong wish to have or do something
source.example: He now had enough money to satisfy all his desires.
examples: He now had enough money to satisfy all his desires.
desire for something a strong desire for power/revenge
desire to do something She has a burning desire to be an artist.
(formal) I have no desire (= I do not want) to discuss the matter further.
He has expressed a desire to see you.
(formal) desire that… his father's desire that he become a lawyer
source.twin_note_ru: desire это сильное, часто страстное желание, книжное, wish это обычное пожелание

source.definition: to want something; to wish for something
source.example: desire something, We all desire health and happiness.
examples: desire something, We all desire health and happiness.
desire something We all desire health and happiness.
The house had everything you could desire.
The dessert can be topped with cream, if desired (= if you like).
The medicine did not achieve the desired effect.
desire to do something Fewer people desire to live in the north of the country.
desire somebody to do something She desired him to leave her alone.
source.twin_note_ru: desire звучит книжно и почти не встречается в речи, want это повседневное «хотеть»

source.definition: that you would like to have or do; worth having or doing
source.example: She chatted for a few minutes about the qualities she considered desirable in a secretary.
examples: She chatted for a few minutes about the qualities she considered desirable in a secretary.
Such measures are desirable, if not essential.
The house has many desirable features.
Experience of computers is highly desirable.
It is desirable that… (British English) It is desirable that interest rates should be reduced.
(especially North American English) It is desirable that interest rates be reduced.
It is desirable (for somebody) (to do something) It is no longer desirable for such young children to take formal written tests.
source.twin_note_ru: desirable это тот, которого стоит хотеть, оценка, desired это тот, которого конкретно хотели

source.definition: the act or ceremony of burying a dead body

examples: a burial place/mound/site

His family insisted he should be given a proper burial.
baptism, marriage and burial services
source.twin_note_ru: burial — сам факт погребения тела в земле, funeral — церемония прощания и похорон.

source.definition: to break open or apart, especially because of pressure from inside; to make something break in this way
source.example: That balloon will burst if you blow it up any more.
examples: That balloon will burst if you blow it up any more.

burst apart There was a danger that the engine would burst apart.
burst something Don't burst that balloon!

a burst pipe

examples: Urban life in the nineteenth century is well documented.

source.twin_note_ru: doctrine это официальное учение церкви, партии или государства, которое принимают на веру, theory это объяснение, которое проверяют и оспаривают

source.definition: the documents that are required for something, or that give evidence or proof of something

examples: I couldn't enter the country because I didn't have all the necessary documentation.

source.definition: connected with the relation of plants and living creatures to each other and to their environment

examples: We risk upsetting the ecological balance of the area.

source.definition: to make objects, patterns, etc. by cutting away material from a piece of wood or stone, or another hard material

source.definition: to succeed in attracting and keeping somebody’s attention and interest

source.definition: a hall in a public building that is used for formal meetings

source.definition: when you think about the true, important or basic nature of somebody/something

source.definition: the most important quality or feature of something, that makes it what it is
source.example: His paintings capture the essence of France.
examples: His paintings capture the essence of France.
in essence In essence (= when you consider the most important points), your situation isn't so different from mine.
source.twin_note_ru: essence: главное свойство, без которого вещь не она, in essence, nature: характер и природа явления в целом, the nature of the problem.

source.definition: a complete lack of order
source.example: economic/political/domestic chaos
examples: economic/political/domestic chaos
Heavy snow has caused total chaos on the roads.
in chaos The house was in chaos after the party.
The country was thrown/plunged into chaos by the president's death.
source.twin_note_ru: chaos неисчисляемое и про полную неуправляемость крупного масштаба; mess про бытовой беспорядок в вещах или делах и может быть исчисляемым (a mess)

source.definition: lasting for a long time; difficult to cure
source.example: chronic bronchitis/arthritis/asthma
examples: chronic bronchitis/arthritis/asthma
source.twin_note_ru: chronic про затяжные болезни и проблемы, всегда с негативной оценкой; constant нейтрально, про непрерывное или частое повторение

source.definition: connected with or located on the outside of something/somebody
source.example: the external walls of the building
examples: the external walls of the building
an external hard drive
The lotion is for external use only (= only for the skin and must not be eaten).
source.twin_note_ru: external формальное, про внешнее для системы: external factors, external drive, а outer про наружный слой.

source.definition: a feeling, situation, way of behaving, etc. that is as different as possible from another or is opposite to it
source.example: extremes of love and hate
examples: extremes of love and hate
He used to be very shy, but now he's gone to the opposite extreme (= changed from one extreme kind of behaviour to another).
She goes from one extreme to the other (= changes from one extreme kind of behaviour to another).

between extremes He takes a position somewhere these two extremes.
source.twin_note_ru: extreme это крайняя точка или крайняя мера, часто во множественном extremes, а limit это граница, за которую нельзя.

source.definition: a person whose opinions, especially about religion or politics, are extreme, and who may do things that are violent or illegal for what they believe
source.example: left-wing/right-wing/political/religious extremists
examples: left-wing/right-wing/political/religious extremists
He was assassinated by extremists.
source.twin_note_ru: extremist готов на крайние, часто насильственные меры, а radical может быть нейтральным сторонником коренных перемен.

headword: in an attempt to do sth

source.definition: a thick, solid piece that has been cut or broken off something
source.example: a chunk of cheese/masonry
examples: a chunk of cheese/masonry
source.twin_note_ru: chunk это крупный плотный кусок, отломанный или отрубленный; piece любая часть, нейтрально и без размера

source.definition: a short fight between two groups of people
source.example: Clashes broke out between police and demonstrators.
examples: Clashes broke out between police and demonstrators.
Eight people were wounded in a clash with border guards.
Several people were injured in violent clashes with the police.
source.twin_note_ru: clash это короткое открытое столкновение или несовпадение (дат, цветов, характеров); conflict это длительное противостояние

source.definition: to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done something wrong or illegal
source.example: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed.
examples: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed.
confess to (doing) something She confessed to the murder.
confess (that)… He confessed that he had stolen the money.
confess to somebody (that)… She confessed to me that she had known his true identity for some time.
confess your crime, error, etc. We persuaded her to confess her crime.
source.twin_note_ru: confess — признаться в вине, грехе или тайне, часто с усилием; admit — нейтрально признать факт.

source.definition: a person who does a job that needs special training and a high level of education
source.example: You need a professional to sort out your finances.
examples: You need a professional to sort out your finances.
Our officers are all highly trained professionals.
source.twin_note_ru: professional — тот, кто зарабатывает этим на жизнь, противоположность любителю; expert — тот, кто глубоко разбирается, независимо от заработка

source.definition: a statement that a person makes, admitting that they are guilty of a crime; the act of making such a statement
source.example: After hours of questioning by police, she made a full confession.
examples: After hours of questioning by police, she made a full confession.

source.twin_note_ru: confession — признание вины или исповедь; admission — признание неудобного факта (и ещё «допуск, вход»).

source.definition: to hold on tightly to somebody/something
source.example: cling to somebody/something, survivors clinging to a raft
examples: cling to somebody/something, survivors clinging to a raft
cling to somebody/something survivors clinging to a raft
Leaves still clung to the branches.
cling on to somebody/something She clung on to her baby.
cling on Cling on tight!
cling together They clung together, shivering with cold.
source.twin_note_ru: cling значит цепляться и не отпускать, часто от страха или привязанности, идёт с to; stick про прилипание и приклеивание предметов

source.definition: a group of things of the same type that grow or appear close together
source.example: The telescope is focused on a dense cluster of stars at the edge of the galaxy.

source.definition: an act of using one person or thing in the place of another
source.example: Two substitutions were made during the game.
examples: Two substitutions were made during the game.
substitution of A for B the substitution of low-fat spreads for butter
substitution of B with A the substitution of butter with low-fat spreads
source.twin_note_ru: Substitution это сам акт подстановки (в спорте, в формуле, в рецепте), replacement чаще сам предмет или человек, пришедший на место.

source.definition: a pattern of straight lines, usually crossing each other to form squares
source.example: New York’s grid of streets
examples: New York’s grid of streets
source.twin_note_ru: grid это регулярная сетка из линий или энергосистема страны; network это сеть связей между людьми, устройствами, компаниями.

source.definition: a very sad feeling, especially when somebody dies
source.example: She was overcome with grief when her husband died.
examples: She was overcome with grief when her husband died.
They were able to share their common joys and griefs.
grief for somebody/something her grief for her dead husband
grief over something grief over the loss of friends
grief at something He could not hide his grief at her death.
source.twin_note_ru: grief это острое горе от утраты, чаще после смерти близкого; sorrow книжная печаль вообще.

source.definition: a period of time when an organized group of employees of a company stops working because of an argument over pay or conditions
source.example: the miners'/firefighters'/teachers' strike
examples: the miners'/firefighters'/teachers' strike
a strike by teachers
a one-day strike
an unofficial strike
Union leaders called a strike.
Air traffic controllers are threatening to go on strike.
Half the workforce are now (out) on strike.
to come out on strike
The train drivers have voted to take strike action.
The student union has called for a rent strike (= a refusal to pay rent as a protest).
source.twin_note_ru: strike это организованная остановка работы (go on strike), protest это любая акция несогласия, работу при этом не бросают

source.definition: to hit somebody/something hard or with force
source.example: strike somebody/something, The ship struck a rock.
examples: strike somebody/something, The ship struck a rock.
strike somebody/something The ship struck a rock.
The child ran into the road and was struck by a car.
The tree was struck by lightning.
Warplanes struck several targets in the city.
strike somebody/something + adv./prep. He fell, striking his head on the edge of the table.
He was struck in the head by a bullet.
The stone struck her on the forehead.
strike against something The oar struck against something hard.
source.twin_note_ru: strike книжнее и часто о внезапном ударе стихии или мысли (lightning struck, it struck me that), hit это обиходное ударить или попасть

source.definition: interesting and unusual enough to attract attention
source.example: a striking feature
examples: a striking feature
She bears a striking resemblance to her older sister.
In striking contrast to their brothers, the girls were both intelligent and charming.
The similarities between the two cases are striking.
source.twin_note_ru: striking значит бросающийся в глаза, поразительный (сходство, контраст, внешность), impressive значит вызывающий восхищение уровнем и качеством

source.definition: to break or press something into very small pieces between two hard surfaces or using a special machine
source.example: to grind coffee/corn
examples: to grind coffee/corn
The animal has teeth that grind its food into a pulp.
source.twin_note_ru: grind это перетирать в порошок трением (grind coffee); crush это раздавить нажимом, форма теряется, но порошка нет.

source.definition: being the total amount of something before anything is taken away
source.example: gross weight (= including the container or wrapping)
examples: gross weight (= including the container or wrapping)
gross income/wage (= before taxes, etc. are taken away)
Investments showed a gross profit of 26 per cent.
The family have three children and a gross income of £50 000.
source.twin_note_ru: gross это сумма до вычетов и противопоставлено net (gross income); total это просто итог по всем позициям.

source.definition: an amount of money
source.example: You will be fined the sum of £200.
examples: You will be fined the sum of £200.
a large sum of money
The judge awarded them an undisclosed six-figure sum in damages.
Huge sums have been invested in this project.
The team has raised substantial sums for local charities.
source.twin_note_ru: Sum это денежная сумма или результат сложения (a large sum of money), amount это количество чего угодно, включая неисчисляемое.
Sum up это разговорный фразовый глагол, подвести итог парой фраз; summarize книжнее и про письменное краткое изложение.

source.definition: the highest point of something, especially the top of a mountain
source.example: We reached the summit at noon.
examples: We reached the summit at noon.
This path leads to the summit.
(figurative) the summit of his career
source.twin_note_ru: Summit это вершина горы и встреча на высшем уровне (G20 summit), peak это пик горы и максимум показателя (peak of demand).

source.definition: a member of a small group of soldiers who are not part of an official army and who fight against official soldiers, usually to try to change the government
source.example: urban guerrillas (= those who fight in towns)
examples: urban guerrillas (= those who fight in towns)
guerrilla war/warfare (= fought by guerrillas on one or both sides)
a guerrilla movement
source.twin_note_ru: guerrilla это партизан и партизанская тактика (guerrilla warfare, guerrilla marketing); partisan в английском чаще значит «пристрастный, партийный».

source.definition: the unhappy feelings caused by knowing or thinking that you have done something wrong
source.example: She had feelings of guilt about leaving her children and going to work.
examples: She had feelings of guilt about leaving her children and going to work.
Many survivors were left with a sense of guilt.
a guilt complex (= an exaggerated sense of guilt)
source.twin_note_ru: guilt это чувство вины и юридическая виновность; fault это вина в смысле «чья ошибка» (it's my fault).

source.definition: a doctor who is trained to perform surgery (= medical operations that involve cutting open a person’s body)
source.example: a brain/heart surgeon
examples: a brain/heart surgeon
Surgeons performed two operations on him yesterday.
source.twin_note_ru: Surgeon это врач, который оперирует; doctor это врач вообще и обращение к нему.

source.definition: medical treatment of injuries or diseases that involves cutting open a person’s body and often removing or replacing some parts; the branch of medicine connected with this treatment
source.example: major/minor surgery
examples: major/minor surgery
to undergo heart/knee/shoulder surgery
He will require surgery on his left knee.
The doctor had to perform emergency surgery to the patient's head.
She's a specialist in reconstructive and cosmetic surgery.
The president is to undergo minor surgery to remove a small growth from his hand.
source.twin_note_ru: Surgery неисчисляемое (have surgery, undergo surgery) и значит хирургию как область, а в британском ещё кабинет врача; operation исчисляемое, have an operation.

source.definition: used in or connected with surgery
source.example: surgical procedures
examples: surgical procedures
a surgical ward (= for patients having operations)
source.twin_note_ru: Surgical только про хирургию и её инструменты, плюс переносное «точечный» (surgical strike); medical про медицину в целом.

source.definition: the tube in the body through which food passes when it leaves the stomach
source.example: It can take up to 72 hours for food to pass through the gut.
examples: It can take up to 72 hours for food to pass through the gut.
I had a terrible pain in my guts after eating too many plums.
source.twin_note_ru: gut это кишечник и «нутро», разговорное (gut feeling, gut bacteria); stomach это желудок как орган.

source.definition: to describe somebody/something as being very good or special, especially in newspapers, etc.
source.example: be hailed (as) something, The conference was hailed as a great success.
examples: be hailed (as) something, The conference was hailed as a great success.
be hailed (as) something The conference was hailed as a great success.
The expedition was widely hailed as a success.
Teenager Matt Brown is being hailed a hero for saving a young child from drowning.
hail somebody/something as something Union leaders hailed the socialists’ victory as a huge step forward.
source.twin_note_ru: hail это книжное «провозглашать, превозносить» (hailed as a hero) или окликнуть такси; greet это обычное поприветствовать при встрече.

source.definition: belonging to the same time
source.example: We have no contemporary account of the battle (= written near the time that it happened).
examples: We have no contemporary account of the battle (= written near the time that it happened).
contemporary with somebody/something He was contemporary with the dramatist Congreve.
The amphitheatre is roughly contemporary with the Colosseum in Rome.
source.twin_note_ru: contemporary это «того же времени, что и» или «самый сегодняшний» (contemporary art), modern это новый в противовес старому

source.definition: in a way that lasts or is intended to last or be used only for a short time; in a way that is not permanent
source.example: We regret this service is temporarily unavailable.
examples: We regret this service is temporarily unavailable.
The company announced that it would be temporarily closing the factory because of the global downturn.

source.definition: lasting or intended to last or be used only for a short time; not permanent
source.example: to hire temporary workers
examples: to hire temporary workers
They had to move into temporary accommodation.
Volunteers built temporary shelters for the survivors.
temporary relief from pain
a temporary fix/measure/solution
More than half the staff are temporary.

source.definition: at an equal distance between two points; in the middle of a period of time
source.example: It's about halfway between London and Bristol.
examples: It's about halfway between London and Bristol.
He left halfway through the ceremony.
I'm afraid we're not even halfway there yet.

source.definition: the act of annoying or worrying somebody by putting pressure on them or saying or doing unpleasant things to them
source.example: sexual/racial harassment
examples: sexual/racial harassment
workplace/street harassment (= that happens at work/in the street)
source.twin_note_ru: harassment это юридический термин о домогательствах и преследовании, чаще на работе; bullying это травля, чаще в школе и без правового смысла.

source.definition: an act of trying to do something, especially something difficult, often with no success
source.example: I passed my driving test at the first attempt.
examples: I passed my driving test at the first attempt.
attempt to do something They made no attempt to escape.
The launch will go ahead despite the failure of previous attempts to create an online business.
Why have repeated attempts to find a permanent solution to the problem failed ?
They were frustrated in their attempts to get an explanation.
He has failed in three previous attempts to win the world title.
in an attempt to do something Two factories were closed in an attempt to cut costs.
attempt at something The couple made an unsuccessful attempt at a compromise.
attempt at doing something They were praised for making an attempt at solving the problem.
source.twin_note_ru: attempt формальнее и часто о серьёзной или неудавшейся попытке (an attempt at/to do), try разговорное (have a try)

source.definition: to make an effort or try to do something, especially something difficult
source.example: attempt to do something, I will attempt to answer all your questions.
examples: attempt to do something, I will attempt to answer all your questions.
attempt to do something I will attempt to answer all your questions.
She never attempted to explain her behaviour to her family.
She has been unsuccessfully attempting to find out the name of the police officer.
I haven't even attempted to do any of this yet.
Do not attempt to repair this yourself.
attempt something The prisoners attempted an escape, but failed.
source.twin_note_ru: attempt только с инфинитивом и о трудном деле, try и с инфинитивом, и с -ing, и в любом бытовом контексте

source.definition: to attract somebody or make somebody want to do or have something, even if they know it is wrong
source.example: tempt somebody, I was tempted by the dessert menu.
examples: tempt somebody, I was tempted by the dessert menu.
tempt somebody I was tempted by the dessert menu.
Don't tempt thieves by leaving valuables clearly visible.
tempt somebody into (doing) something He was tempted into a life of crime.
tempt somebody to do something I was tempted to take the day off.
source.twin_note_ru: tempt про соблазн чем-то заманчивым, часто в пассиве (be tempted to), seduce про целенаправленное обольщение, обычно сексуальное

source.definition: the machines and electronic parts in a computer or other electronic system
source.example: We supply computer hardware to businesses.
examples: We supply computer hardware to businesses.
source.twin_note_ru: hardware это «железо» компьютера в противовес software, а также скобяные товары; equipment это оборудование вообще, любое.

source.definition: a state of peaceful existence and agreement
source.example: social/racial harmony
examples: social/racial harmony
in harmony They lived together in perfect harmony.
in harmony with something the need to be in harmony with our environment

source.definition: an idea or explanation of something that is based on a few known facts but that has not yet been proved to be true or correct
source.example: to formulate/confirm a hypothesis
examples: to formulate/confirm a hypothesis
a hypothesis about the function of dreams
There is little evidence to support these hypotheses.
source.root_meaning_ru: положение, то, что поставлено (греч. tithenai — класть)
source.twin_note_ru: hypothesis — предположение, которое ещё предстоит проверить; theory — объяснение, уже подкреплённое данными

source.definition: a long piece of writing completed by a student as part of a university degree, based on their own research
source.example: Students must submit a thesis on an agreed subject within four years.
examples: Students must submit a thesis on an agreed subject within four years.
source.twin_note_ru: thesis это ещё и главное утверждение, которое доказывают в тексте, dissertation только письменная квалификационная работа

source.definition: the act of combining separate ideas, beliefs, styles, etc.; a mixture or combination of ideas, beliefs, styles, etc.
source.example: synthesis of A with B, the synthesis of art with everyday life
examples: synthesis of A with B, the synthesis of art with everyday life
synthesis of A with B the synthesis of art with everyday life
synthesis of A and B a synthesis of traditional and modern values

source.definition: cruel, severe and unkind
source.example: The punishment was harsh and unfair.
examples: The punishment was harsh and unfair.
The minister received some harsh criticism.
the harsh treatment of prisoners
He regretted his harsh words.
We had to face up to the harsh realities of life sooner or later.
It may seem harsh to criticize him after his death.
‘She's just totally useless!’ ‘That's a bit harsh.’
source.twin_note_ru: harsh — резкий и грубый по ощущению (criticism, words, winter, light), с эмоциональной оценкой; severe — нейтральнее и формальнее, о степени тяжести (severe injury, severe shortage).

source.definition: a very strong feeling of dislike for somebody/something
source.example: He looked at me with intense hatred.
examples: He looked at me with intense hatred.
There was fear and hatred in his voice.
hatred for somebody/something She felt nothing but hatred for her attacker.
hatred of somebody/something a profound hatred of war
hatred towards somebody feelings of hatred towards the bombers
racial hatred (= hatred for people from a different race)
The debate simply revived old hatreds.
source.twin_note_ru: hatred — обычное существительное «ненависть» (hatred of/for); hate как существительное живёт в устойчивых сочетаниях: hate speech, hate crime.

source.definition: to measure how long it takes for something to happen or for somebody to do something
source.example: time something, ‘How long does it take to get to Leeds from here?’ ‘I don’t know, I’ve never timed it.’
examples: time something, ‘How long does it take to get to Leeds from here?’ ‘I don’t know, I’ve never timed it.’
time something ‘How long does it take to get to Leeds from here?’ ‘I don’t know, I’ve never timed it.’
time something at something The winner was timed at 20.4 seconds.
time how long… Time how long it takes you to run ten laps.
Time how long it takes you to answer the questions.
source.twin_note_ru: time значит подгадать момент или засечь время; schedule значит поставить в расписание на конкретную дату.

source.definition: the act of choosing when something happens; a particular point or period of time when something happens or is planned
source.example: The timing of the decision was a complete surprise.
examples: The timing of the decision was a complete surprise.
Please check your flight timings carefully.
source.twin_note_ru: timing это выбор момента и то, насколько он удачен (bad timing); time это время как отрезок или момент на часах.

source.definition: happening at exactly the right time
source.example: A nasty incident was prevented by the timely arrival of the police.
examples: A nasty incident was prevented by the timely arrival of the police.
This has been a timely reminder to us all.
I was grateful for your timely intervention.
All claims must be dealt with in a professional and timely manner.
The timely intervention of a teacher meant a fight was avoided.
source.twin_note_ru: timely про событие, которое пришлось кстати и вовремя (a timely warning); punctual про человека, который не опаздывает.

source.definition: if the ghost of a dead person haunts a place, people say that they have seen it there
source.example: A headless rider haunts the country lanes.
examples: A headless rider haunts the country lanes.
I’ll come back to haunt you!
source.twin_note_ru: haunt преследует мысленно — воспоминания, вина, призраки; физическую погоню передают pursue и chase.

source.definition: something that can be dangerous or cause damage
source.example: a fire/safety hazard
examples: a fire/safety hazard
hazard to somebody/something Growing levels of pollution represent a serious health hazard to the local population.
hazard of (doing) something Everybody is aware of the hazards of smoking.
source.twin_note_ru: hazard — конкретный источник опасности, термин техники и охраны труда (fire hazard, health hazard); danger — опасность вообще (in danger).

source.definition: very surprising; difficult to believe
source.example: She ran 100m in an astonishing 10.6 seconds.
examples: She ran 100m in an astonishing 10.6 seconds.
I find it absolutely astonishing that you didn't like it.
source.root_meaning_ru: греметь, гром (лат. tonare; extonare — поражать как громом)
source.twin_note_ru: astonishing — поражающий так, что трудно поверить, книжнее и сильнее, amazing — восторженное разговорное «потрясающий», часто просто «очень хороший»

source.definition: the quality of somebody’s voice, especially expressing a particular emotion
source.example: speaking in hushed/low/clipped/measured, etc. tones
examples: speaking in hushed/low/clipped/measured, etc. tones
a conversational tone
a tone of surprise
Don't speak to me in that tone of voice (= in that unpleasant way).
There's not need to take that tone (= speak critically or rudely) with me—it's not my fault we're late.
source.twin_note_ru: tone это общая тональность цвета или голоса (warm tones, an angry tone); shade это конкретный оттенок одного цвета, светлее или темнее.

source.definition: a series of musical notes that are sung or played in a particular order to form a piece of music
source.example: to sing/whistle a tune
examples: to sing/whistle a tune
He was humming a familiar tune.
I can play a few tunes on the piano.
I don't know the title but I recognize the tune.
It was a catchy tune (= easy to remember).
to the tune of something a football song sung to the tune of (= using the tune of) ‘When the saints go marching in’
a show/dance/pop tune
source.twin_note_ru: tune это мотив, который можно напеть или узнать, melody это мелодия как музыкальный термин

source.definition: receiving or involving a lot of attention and discussion in the media
source.example: a high-profile campaign
examples: a high-profile campaign
source.twin_note_ru: high-profile — громкий, в центре внимания прессы, сочетается с делами и событиями (high-profile case, client); famous — широко известный, обычно о людях.

source.definition: the furthest that you can see, where the sky seems to meet the land or the sea
source.example: The sun sank below the horizon.
examples: The sun sank below the horizon.
A ship appeared on the horizon.

source.definition: to change the shape, appearance or sound of something so that it is strange or not clear
source.example: a fairground mirror that distorts your shape
examples: a fairground mirror that distorts your shape
The loudspeaker seemed to distort his voice.
source.twin_note_ru: distort искажает смысл, факты, звук, изображение, twist буквально скручивает предмет, а в переносном значении разговорнее

source.definition: the act of causing somebody severe pain in order to punish them or make them say or do something
source.example: Many of the refugees have suffered torture.
examples: Many of the refugees have suffered torture.
the use of torture
terrible instruments of torture
under torture His confessions were made under torture.
I heard stories of gruesome tortures in prisons.
source.twin_note_ru: torture это пытка, боль причиняют намеренно; suffering это страдание само по себе, виновника может и не быть.

source.definition: to hurt somebody physically or mentally in order to punish them or make them tell you something
source.example: torture somebody, Many of the rebels were captured and tortured by secret police.
examples: torture somebody, Many of the rebels were captured and tortured by secret police.
torture somebody Many of the rebels were captured and tortured by secret police.
The prisoners were routinely tortured.
torture somebody into doing something He was tortured into giving them the information.
source.twin_note_ru: torture значит долго и намеренно мучить ради признания или наказания; hurt значит причинить боль, в том числе нечаянно.

source.definition: a hard pointed part that grows, usually in pairs, on the heads of some animals, such as sheep and cows. Horns are often curved.
source.example: a large bull with curved horns
examples: a large bull with curved horns
source.twin_note_ru: horn — постоянный рог (бык, коза), а также духовой инструмент и автомобильный сигнал; antler — ветвистые рога оленя, которые сбрасываются

source.definition: a person who is captured and held prisoner by a person or group, and who may be injured or killed if people do not do what the person or group is asking
source.example: Three children were taken hostage during the bank robbery.
examples: Three children were taken hostage during the bank robbery.
He was held hostage for almost a year.
The government is negotiating the release of the hostages.
The hijackers kept the pilot as a hostage on board the plane.
The gunmen took 24 hostages.
diplomatic efforts to get the hostages released
source.twin_note_ru: hostage — удерживают ради выкупа или требований; prisoner — заключённый или военнопленный

source.definition: a long line or series of marks that is left by somebody/something
source.example: a trail of blood
examples: a trail of blood
tourists who leave a trail of litter everywhere they go
The hurricane left a trail of destruction behind it.
source.twin_note_ru: trail — протоптанная тропа в лесу или горах, маршрут; path — любая дорожка, в том числе в парке и в переносном смысле «путь».

source.definition: to pull something behind somebody/something, usually along the ground; to be pulled along in this way
source.example: trail something, A jeep trailing a cloud of dust was speeding in my direction.
examples: trail something, A jeep trailing a cloud of dust was speeding in my direction.
trail something A jeep trailing a cloud of dust was speeding in my direction.
I trailed my hand in the water as the boat moved along.
(+ adv./prep.) The bride's dress trailed behind her.
source.twin_note_ru: trail — тянуться следом и отставать (в том числе проигрывать в счёте); follow — нейтрально идти за кем-то или следовать правилу.

source.definition: a truck, or a container with wheels, that is pulled by another vehicle
source.example: a car towing a trailer with a boat on it
examples: a car towing a trailer with a boat on it
source.twin_note_ru: trailer — полноценный ролик-анонс фильма на 1-2 минуты, а также прицеп; teaser — короткая дразнилка, которая выходит раньше трейлера.

source.definition: showing you do not think that you are as important as other people
source.example: Be humble enough to learn from your mistakes.
examples: Be humble enough to learn from your mistakes.
my humble tribute to this great man
source.twin_note_ru: humble — скромный без гордыни, а также «простой, небогатый» (humble home); modest — сдержанный в оценке себя и умеренный по размеру

source.definition: the belief that somebody/something is good, sincere, honest, etc. and will not try to harm or trick you
source.example: Our partnership is based on trust.
examples: Our partnership is based on trust.
This is a relationship built on mutual trust.
It has taken years to earn their trust.
We worked hard to gain the trust of local people.
Talking openly with your team helps to build trust.
trust in somebody/something Her trust in him was unfounded.
If you put your trust in me, I will not let you down.
I want to thank all those people who have placed their trust in me.
She will not betray your trust (= do something that you have asked her not to do).
He was appointed to a position of trust (= a job involving a lot of responsibility, because people trust him).
This is a serious breach of trust.
The company has to earn the trust and confidence of consumers again.
trust between somebody and somebody There is a lack of trust between the two countries.
source.twin_note_ru: trust это доверие к человеку или организации, confidence это уверенность в результате или в себе

source.definition: to have confidence in somebody; to believe that somebody is good, sincere, honest, etc.
source.example: trust somebody, She trusts Alan implicitly.
examples: trust somebody, She trusts Alan implicitly.
trust somebody She trusts Alan implicitly.
He has shown that he can't be trusted.
Never trust a man who will not look you in the eye.
a trusted adviser/friend
trust somebody to do something You can trust me not to tell anyone.
She nodded, not trusting herself to speak.
Which party do you trust to run the economy?
source.twin_note_ru: trust somebody значит полагаться на человека, believe somebody значит верить, что он говорит правду

source.definition: a person or an organization that has control of money or property that has been put into a trust for somebody

punch somebody/something in/on something She punched him on the nose.
source.twin_note_ru: punch — ударить именно кулаком, сильно; hit — ударить любым способом или попасть по цели.

source.definition: a sum of money that is given by the government or by another organization to be used for a particular purpose
source.example: government/federal grants
examples: government/federal grants
There is a lot of competition for research grants.
student grants (= to pay for their education)
to apply for a grant
a grant application
grant to somebody/something The money is used for small grants to deserving organizations.
grant from somebody/something The study was supported by a grant from the National Science Foundation.
grant for something The government has awarded a grant for the restoration of the building.
grant of something The provincial government provided a start-up grant of $11 400
grant to do something The school has received a large grant to improve its buildings.
source.twin_note_ru: grant это целевые деньги на проект или исследование от фонда, государства, университета; scholarship это деньги конкретному студенту на учёбу.

source.definition: to agree to give somebody what they ask for, especially formal or legal permission to do something
source.example: grant something, My request was granted.
examples: grant something, My request was granted.
grant something My request was granted.
the rights expressly granted by the terms of the lease
The judge granted an injunction preventing the newspaper from printing the names.
grant somebody something I was granted permission to visit the palace.
She was granted a divorce.
The court granted him leave to appeal.
He was granted a licence to mine in the area.
The bank finally granted me a £500 loan.
grant something to somebody/something The bank finally granted a £500 loan to me.
These lands had been granted to the family in perpetuity.
source.twin_note_ru: grant формальное: инстанция сверху даёт право, разрешение, деньги (grant access, grant a visa); provide нейтральное «обеспечивать чем-то».

source.definition: a limited number or amount of people or things that is officially allowed
source.example: to introduce a strict import quota on grain
examples: to introduce a strict import quota on grain
source.twin_note_ru: quota - выделенная кому-то доля или норма (импортная, по найму), limit - просто предел, который нельзя переходить.

source.definition: connected with drawings and design, especially in the production of books, magazines, websites, etc.
source.example: graphic design
examples: graphic design
a graphic designer
source.twin_note_ru: graphic о натуралистично подробном, часто неприятном описании (graphic violence); vivid о ярком живом образе без негативного оттенка.

source.definition: designs, drawings or pictures that are used especially in the production of books, magazines, websites, etc.
source.example: Text and graphics are prepared separately and then combined.
examples: Text and graphics are prepared separately and then combined.
The program can produce and manipulate text and graphics.
The screen can display simple graphics as well as text.
source.twin_note_ru: graphics это изображения и графика в целом, неисчисляемое; graph это один конкретный график или диаграмма, исчисляемое.

source.definition: a system that uses radio waves to find the position and movement of objects, for example planes and ships, when they cannot be seen
source.example: They located the ship by radar.
examples: They located the ship by radar.
a radar screen

source.definition: a strong hold of somebody/something or control over somebody/something
source.example: I grabbed him, but he slipped from my grasp.
examples: I grabbed him, but he slipped from my grasp.
She felt a firm grasp on her arm.
Don't let the situation escape from your grasp.
As soon as he relaxed his grasp on the rope, it was pulled out of his hands.
source.twin_note_ru: grasp чаще о понимании (a good grasp of English); grip о физической хватке и контроле над ситуацией.

source.definition: to take a strong hold of somebody/something
source.example: He grasped my hand and shook it warmly.
examples: He grasped my hand and shook it warmly.
Kay grasped him by the wrist.
source.twin_note_ru: grab это быстро выхватить рывком; grasp это крепко обхватить, а также «уловить смысл», чего у grab нет.

source.definition: relating to the most basic and important parts of something; complete and detailed
source.example: the need for radical changes in education
examples: the need for radical changes in education
demands for radical reform of the law
radical differences between the two systems
This document marks a radical departure from earlier recommendations.
source.twin_note_ru: radical - затрагивающий самую основу (radical change, radical views), extreme - о крайней степени чего угодно.

source.definition: to tell somebody that you are pleased about their success or achievements
source.example: I congratulated them all on their results.
examples: I congratulated them all on their results.
The authors are to be congratulated on producing such a clear and authoritative work.
source.twin_note_ru: congratulate — адресовано человеку: congratulate somebody on something; celebrate — про само событие, которое отмечают.

source.definition: an attractive quality of movement that is smooth and done with control; a simple and beautiful quality
source.example: She moves with the natural grace of a ballerina.
examples: She moves with the natural grace of a ballerina.
a debut album of uncommon grace and beauty
source.twin_note_ru: grace — плавность движений и милость, благосклонность (with grace, say grace); elegance — изящество стиля, вкуса и внешнего вида.

source.definition: a feeling of violent anger that is difficult to control
source.example: His face was dark with rage.
examples: His face was dark with rage.
to be shaking/trembling/speechless with rage
in a rage Sue stormed out of the room in a rage.
He flies into a rage if you even mention the subject.
source.twin_note_ru: rage - ярость, сильнее и неуправляемее; anger - обычная злость любой силы.

source.definition: very serious and important; giving you a reason to feel worried
source.example: The police have expressed grave concern about the missing child's safety.
examples: The police have expressed grave concern about the missing child's safety.
The consequences will be very grave if nothing is done.
We were in grave danger.
I fear you are making a very grave mistake.
source.twin_note_ru: grave книжное и только о по-настоящему опасном или мрачном (grave danger, grave concerns); serious нейтральное и сочетается почти со всем.

source.definition: the force that attracts objects in space towards each other, and that on the earth pulls them towards the centre of the planet, so that things fall to the ground when they are dropped
source.example: Newton’s law of gravity
examples: Newton’s law of gravity
source.twin_note_ru: gravity в значении «серьёзность» книжное и только о тяжёлых ситуациях (the gravity of the crisis); seriousness нейтрально и шире.

source.definition: quickly and without difficulty
source.example: All ingredients are readily available from your local store.
examples: All ingredients are readily available from your local store.
source.twin_note_ru: readily значит охотно, без колебаний, и «без труда» в связках вроде readily available; easily это просто «легко» о любом действии

source.definition: a wide smile
source.example: She gave a broad grin.
examples: She gave a broad grin.
a wry/sheepish grin
with a grin ‘No,’ he said with a grin.
source.twin_note_ru: grin это широкая улыбка во весь рот, с зубами; smile это любая улыбка, в том числе еле заметная.

source.definition: to smile widely
source.example: They grinned with delight when they heard our news.
examples: They grinned with delight when they heard our news.
Stop grinning and tell me what happened!
grin at somebody She grinned amiably at us.
grin something He grinned a wide grin.
source.twin_note_ru: grin это ухмыляться или широко скалиться, часто с оттенком озорства; smile нейтрально улыбаться.

source.definition: to say or do something that makes somebody less frightened or worried
source.example: reassure somebody (about something), They tried to reassure her, but she still felt anxious.
examples: reassure somebody (about something), They tried to reassure her, but she still felt anxious.
reassure somebody (about something) They tried to reassure her, but she still felt anxious.
reassure somebody that… The doctor reassured him that there was nothing seriously wrong.
be reassured of something She needed to be reassured of his love for her.
source.twin_note_ru: reassure значит снять чужую тревогу, успокоить сомневающегося, assure значит твёрдо заверить, что факт верен

source.definition: an act of holding somebody/something tightly; a particular way of doing this
source.example: Keep a tight grip on the rope.
examples: Keep a tight grip on the rope.
to loosen/release/relax your grip
She tried to get a grip on the icy rock.
The climber slipped and lost her grip.
She struggled from his grip.
Try adjusting your grip on the racket.
source.twin_note_ru: grip это физическая хватка и контроль (lose your grip, get a grip); grasp чаще о понимании предмета.

source.definition: to hold something tightly
source.example: grip something, ‘Please don't go,’ he said, gripping her arm.
examples: grip something, ‘Please don't go,’ he said, gripping her arm.
grip something ‘Please don't go,’ he said, gripping her arm.
grip on to something She gripped on to the railing with both hands.
source.twin_note_ru: grip это сжимать крепко и напряжённо, а также захватывать внимание (a gripping story); hold просто держать.

source.definition: an image in a mirror, on a shiny surface, on water, etc.
source.example: He admired his reflection in the mirror.
examples: He admired his reflection in the mirror.
source.twin_note_ru: reflection это отражение в зеркале или воде, а также размышление; image это изображение или образ сам по себе

source.definition: a formal promise that you will do something or that something will happen
source.example: They are demanding certain guarantees before they sign the treaty.
examples: They are demanding certain guarantees before they sign the treaty.
guarantee of something to give a guarantee of good behaviour
guarantee (that…) He gave me a guarantee that it would never happen again.
source.twin_note_ru: guarantee это обещание или гарантия чего угодно; warranty это юридический гарантийный документ на товар.

source.definition: to promise to do something; to promise something will happen
source.example: guarantee something, Basic human rights, including freedom of speech, are now guaranteed.
examples: guarantee something, Basic human rights, including freedom of speech, are now guaranteed.
guarantee something Basic human rights, including freedom of speech, are now guaranteed.
They told aid workers to leave, saying they could not guarantee their safety.
I personally guarantee total and immediate support in all measures undertaken.
guarantee (that)… We cannot guarantee (that) our flights will never be delayed.
guarantee somebody something The ticket will guarantee you free entry.
guarantee to do something We guarantee to deliver your goods within a week.
source.twin_note_ru: guarantee значит брать на себя обязательство перед кем-то и отвечать за результат; ensure значит проследить, чтобы нужное произошло.

source.definition: an act of saying or showing that you will not do, give or accept something
source.example: the refusal of a request/an invitation/an offer
examples: the refusal of a request/an invitation/an offer
a blunt/flat/curt refusal
refusal to do something His refusal to discuss the matter is very annoying.
source.twin_note_ru: refusal это отказ самому что-то сделать или принять (a refusal to sign), rejection это отклонение чужой заявки, кандидата, человека

source.definition: a set of rules or instructions that are given by an official organization telling you how to do something, especially something difficult
source.example: The government has drawn up guidelines for schools during the pandemic.
examples: The government has drawn up guidelines for schools during the pandemic.
source.twin_note_ru: guideline это рекомендация, отступить можно; rule это обязательное правило, за нарушение есть последствия.

source.definition: help or advice that is given to somebody, especially by somebody older or with more experience
source.example: guidance for teachers on how to use video in the classroom
examples: guidance for teachers on how to use video in the classroom
under the guidance of somebody Activities all take place under the guidance of an experienced tutor.
The helpline was set up for young people in need of guidance and support.
source.twin_note_ru: guidance это системное наставление или официальные указания, неисчисляемое; advice это конкретный совет, тоже неисчисляемое, но бытовое.

source.definition: hesitating before doing something because you do not want to do it or because you are not sure that it is the right thing to do
source.example: He finally gave a reluctant smile.
examples: He finally gave a reluctant smile.
They nodded in reluctant agreement.
reluctant to do something She was reluctant to admit she was wrong.
a reluctant hero (= a person who does not want to be called a hero)
source.twin_note_ru: reluctant — внутренне сопротивляется, но обычно всё же делает (reluctant to agree); unwilling — просто не хочет и может отказаться совсем.

source.definition: the place where a particular type of animal or plant is normally found
source.example: The panda's natural habitat is the bamboo forest.
examples: The panda's natural habitat is the bamboo forest.
The marshes provide a rich habitat for water plants.
the destruction of wildlife habitat
source.twin_note_ru: habitat это естественная среда обитания конкретного вида; environment это окружающая среда вообще, в том числе городская и рабочая.

source.definition: a person or an animal that lives in a particular place
source.example: the oldest inhabitant of the village
examples: the oldest inhabitant of the village
It is a town of about 10 000 inhabitants.
source.twin_note_ru: inhabitant — житель местности в описаниях и статистике (a city of two million inhabitants); resident — официально проживающий по конкретному адресу.

source.definition: a way of dealing with or improving an unpleasant or difficult situation
source.example: When the reservoir becomes blocked, the only remedy lies in cleaning the entire system.
examples: When the reservoir becomes blocked, the only remedy lies in cleaning the entire system.
remedy for something There is no simple remedy for unemployment.
remedy to something There are a number of possible remedies to this problem.
source.twin_note_ru: remedy — средство от проблемы, часто домашнее или юридическое; cure — то, что действительно излечивает болезнь до конца.

source.definition: an act of stopping the movement or progress of somebody/something
source.example: Work came to a halt when the machine broke down.
examples: Work came to a halt when the machine broke down.
The thought brought her to an abrupt halt.
The car skidded to a halt.
Strikes have led to a halt in production.
They decided it was time to call a halt to the project (= stop it officially).
source.twin_note_ru: halt это резкая полная остановка, почти всегда в оборотах come to a halt, bring to a halt; stop нейтрально и свободно сочетается.

source.definition: to stop; to make somebody/something stop
source.example: She walked towards him and then halted.
examples: She walked towards him and then halted.
‘Halt!’ the Major ordered (= used as a command to soldiers).
halt somebody/something The police were halting traffic on the parade route.
The trial was halted after the first week.
source.twin_note_ru: halt формальное, о процессах и производстве в новостях и документах (halt production); stop обычное слово на каждый день.

source.definition: something that makes you think about or remember somebody/something, that you have forgotten or would like to forget
source.example: reminder of something, The sheer size of the cathedral is a constant reminder of the power of religion.
examples: reminder of something, The sheer size of the cathedral is a constant reminder of the power of religion.
reminder of something The sheer size of the cathedral is a constant reminder of the power of religion.
The incident served as a timely reminder of just how dangerous mountaineering can be.
reminder that… The article concludes with a chilling reminder that the disease can strike anyone at any time.
source.twin_note_ru: reminder — напоминание о том, что нужно сделать, заранее и по времени; notification — уведомление о том, что уже произошло.

source.definition: the time of year when the crops are gathered in on a farm, etc.; the act of cutting and gathering crops
source.example: harvest time
examples: harvest time
Farmers are extremely busy during the harvest.
source.twin_note_ru: harvest — сбор урожая как сезон и его итог (a good harvest), crop — сама культура на поле или её объём (wheat crop).

source.definition: to cut and gather a crop; to catch a number of animals or fish to eat
source.example: The nuts are ready to harvest in September.
examples: The nuts are ready to harvest in September.
source.twin_note_ru: harvest — нейтральное «убирать урожай» и о сборе данных; reap книжное и чаще переносное (reap the benefits).

source.definition: to cause somebody/something to be in a particular state or condition
source.example: to render something harmless/useless/ineffective
examples: to render something harmless/useless/ineffective
Hundreds of people were rendered homeless by the earthquake.
source.twin_note_ru: render — книжное «привести в состояние» (render it useless) или «оказать услугу»; make — обычное «сделать каким-то» в живой речи.

source.definition: to stick to something
source.example: Once in the bloodstream, the bacteria adhere to the surface of the red cells.
examples: Once in the bloodstream, the bacteria adhere to the surface of the red cells.
Clean the surface first, or the paint will not adhere.
There was oil adhering to the bird’s feathers.
The tiles may not adhere properly if you do not use the correct glue.
source.twin_note_ru: adhere книжное и требует to: adhere to the rules, stick разговорное и чаще про физическое прилипание

source.definition: that is a basic or permanent part of somebody/something and that cannot be removed
source.example: the difficulties inherent in a study of this type
examples: the difficulties inherent in a study of this type
Violence is inherent in our society.
an inherent weakness in the design of the machine
source.twin_note_ru: inherent — неотделимо присущий самой вещи, обычно inherent in sth; natural — естественный, свойственный по природе, но отделимый.

source.definition: to begin something again after it stopped or was interrupted
source.example: The army renewed its assault on the capital.
examples: The army renewed its assault on the capital.
We have to renew our efforts to attract young players.
The annual dinner is a chance to renew acquaintance with old friends.
source.twin_note_ru: renew — продлить срок действия (подписку, договор, паспорт) или возобновить прерванное; update — обновить содержимое до актуального.

source.definition: to receive money, property, etc. from somebody when they die
source.example: inherit something from somebody, She inherited a fortune from her father.
examples: inherit something from somebody, She inherited a fortune from her father.
inherit something from somebody She inherited a fortune from her father.
inherit (something) He will inherit the title on the death of his uncle.
Does he know that she stands to inherit?

source.definition: the history, traditions, buildings and objects that a country or society has had for many years and that are considered an important part of its character
source.example: Spain’s rich cultural heritage
examples: Spain’s rich cultural heritage
The building is part of our national heritage.
source.twin_note_ru: heritage — культурное наследие народа, передаваемое поколениями (world heritage site); legacy — то, что оставил после себя конкретный человек или эпоха, часто с оценкой.

source.definition: famous and respected
source.example: a renowned author
examples: a renowned author
We asked for advice from the renowned legal expert, Sam Pincher.
renowned as something It is renowned as one of the region's best restaurants.
renowned for something She is renowned for her patience.
source.twin_note_ru: renowned — книжное, о заслуженной известности в своей области (renowned for smth); famous — нейтральное, просто широко известный.

source.definition: the highest level or number
source.example: to hit/reach a high
examples: to hit/reach a high
Exports are currently at record highs.
Profits reached an all-time high last year.
source.twin_note_ru: high — рекордный уровень (hit a new high) или эйфория; peak — вершина, высшая точка графика или карьеры.

source.definition: if a feeling or an effect heightens, or something heightens it, it becomes stronger or increases
source.example: Tension has heightened after the recent bomb attack.
examples: Tension has heightened after the recent bomb attack.
heighten something The campaign is intended to heighten public awareness of the disease.
His breakdown was followed by a period of heightened activity.
Fears of a pandemic were heightened by rising case numbers.
The drug is said to give users a heightened sense of well-being.
source.twin_note_ru: heighten сочетается с абстрактным (tension, awareness, risk, fears), increase — с количеством и числами.

source.definition: the amount of money that you pay to use something for a particular period of time
source.example: Telephone charges include line rental.
examples: Telephone charges include line rental.
source.twin_note_ru: rental — арендная плата или сам арендуемый объект, чаще о короткой аренде (машина, жильё); lease — долгосрочный договор аренды.

source.definition: something that you say or do in an indirect way in order to show somebody what you are thinking
source.example: He gave a broad hint (= one that was obvious) that he was thinking of retiring.
examples: He gave a broad hint (= one that was obvious) that he was thinking of retiring.
Should I drop a hint (= give a hint) to Matt?
He resented any hint that he might be to blame.
source.twin_note_ru: hint — намёк, который кто-то дал специально (drop a hint), а также совет-подсказка; clue — улика или зацепка, ведущая к разгадке.

source.definition: to suggest something in an indirect way
source.example: hint at something, What are you hinting at?
examples: hint at something, What are you hinting at?
hint at something What are you hinting at?
hint (that)… They hinted (that) there might be more job losses.
+ speech ‘I might know something about it,’ he hinted.
source.twin_note_ru: hint at something — человек намекает сознательно; imply — из слов или фактов следует вывод, часто без умысла.

source.definition: the act of replacing one thing with another, especially something that is newer or better
source.example: the replacement of worn car parts
examples: the replacement of worn car parts
source.twin_note_ru: replacement — замена насовсем: новый предмет или человек на освободившееся место; substitute — временная подмена или заменитель.

source.definition: the action of holding somebody/something; the way you are holding somebody/something
source.example: hold on somebody/something, His hold on her arm tightened.
examples: hold on somebody/something, His hold on her arm tightened.
hold on somebody/something His hold on her arm tightened.
He lost his hold on the rock and was swept away by the tide.
Make sure you've got a steady hold on the camera.
She tried to keep hold of the child's hand.
source.twin_note_ru: hold — владение и контроль, живёт в оборотах (get hold of, on hold, take hold); grip — плотность и сила самого хвата.

source.definition: to support something that you think is right and make sure that it continues to exist
source.example: We have a duty to uphold the law.
examples: We have a duty to uphold the law.
The regime has been criticized for failing to uphold human rights.
We are determined to uphold the law.
source.twin_note_ru: uphold значит официально поддержать решение, закон или принцип, часто о суде, support значит поддерживать в любом смысле, включая помощь человеку

source.definition: a country that is governed by a president and politicians elected by the people and where there is no king or queen
source.example: newly independent republics
examples: newly independent republics
Mary McAleese has been the President of the Republic of Ireland since 1997.
source.twin_note_ru: republic — устройство государства без монарха, с выборным главой; democracy — принцип власти народа, возможный и при монархии

source.definition: having no home, and therefore typically living on the streets
source.example: The scheme has been set up to help homeless people.
examples: The scheme has been set up to help homeless people.
The local authority ruled that he had made himself intentionally homeless and was therefore not entitled to be rehoused.
Three hundred people were left homeless by the earthquake.
source.twin_note_ru: homeless — о людях (homeless people, the homeless); о бездомных животных говорят stray (stray dog).

source.definition: the country where a person was born
source.example: Many refugees have been forced to flee their homeland.
examples: Many refugees have been forced to flee their homeland.
source.twin_note_ru: homeland нейтрально и встречается в официальных названиях (Homeland Security); motherland звучит пафосно и патриотически.

source.definition: to look like or be similar to another person or thing
source.example: She closely resembles her sister.
examples: She closely resembles her sister.
So many hotels resemble each other.
The plant resembles grass in appearance.
source.twin_note_ru: resemble идёт прямо с объектом без предлога и говорит о внешнем сходстве, remind требует конструкции remind somebody of something

source.definition: great respect for somebody
source.example: the guest of honour (= the most important one)
examples: the guest of honour (= the most important one)
the seat/place of honour (= given to the most important guest)
They stood in silence as a mark of honour to her.
do honour to somebody/something This biography does great honour to the poet's achievements.
source.twin_note_ru: honour — честь и высокая почесть, о репутации и моральных принципах; respect — обычное уважение к человеку

source.definition: to do something that shows great respect for somebody/something
source.example: honour somebody/something, our honoured guests
examples: honour somebody/something, our honoured guests
honour somebody/something our honoured guests
It was a simple ceremony to honour the Goddess of water.
Actors and musicians gathered to honour the memory of the late singer.
honour somebody with something The President honoured us with a personal visit.
(ironic) I'm glad to see that you've decided to honour us with your presence!
source.twin_note_ru: honour — торжественно чтить, награждать, а также выполнять обязательство (honour a contract); respect — просто уважать

source.definition: to bring or get something back, especially from a place where it should not be
source.example: retrieve something from somebody/something, She bent to retrieve her comb from the floor.
examples: retrieve something from somebody/something, She bent to retrieve her comb from the floor.
retrieve something from somebody/something She bent to retrieve her comb from the floor.

source.definition: the quality of being willing to accept or tolerate somebody/something, especially opinions or behaviour that you may not agree with, or people who are not like you

source.definition: the way that something is spread or exists over a particular area or among a particular group of people
